pending_interview.category: System design (ML/AI-specific) — RAG at scale, eval pipeline design, recommendation systems, agent platforms, feature store design
pending_interview.question: You are building a RAG system — Retrieval-Augmented Generation, meaning an AI system that answers questions by first retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base, then passing those documents to a language model to generate a response — for a large enterprise with roughly 10 million internal documents spanning legal contracts, HR policies, product specs, and engineering runbooks. Users are asking highly varied questions, and early tests show that retrieval quality (finding the right documents before the model even sees them) is the main bottleneck, not the language model itself. Walk through how you would design the retrieval layer at this scale: what would your indexing strategy look like, how would you handle the fact that different document types may need very different retrieval approaches, how would you measure whether retrieval is actually getting better or worse over time, and what failure modes in retrieval would be hardest to detect in production?
